hints.title: Exact Equal Sum K-Partition Obstacle
hints.text: Splitting nums into k subsets of equal sum requires total sum to be divisible by k and each subset to reach target sum // k. How can state bitmasking track consumed elements without redundant state recomputation?

hints.title: Modulo Accumulation State Invariant
hints.text: The current subset sum is uniquely determined by current sum modulo target, so any valid bitmask of chosen numbers either completes a subset or continues toward the next subset.

hints.title: Bitmask Subset Reachability Procedure
hints.text: Check if total sum is divisible by k; if not return false. Sort nums in descending order. Use a bitmask table of size 1 << n tracking the current subset accumulation for each visited mask (-1 for invalid). From a valid mask, transition by picking an unused element that does not exceed the remaining capacity for the current subset. Return whether mask (1 << n) - 1 is reached.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of nums array (1 <= N <= 16)
complexity.notes: Iterates through 2^N bitmask states with at most N transitions each.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Backtracking without bitmask state caching retries equivalent unassigned partitions.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Array of size 2^N stores subset accumulation per mask for N <= 16.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Sorting in descending order to break early when nums[i] > rem.
